reason: The text shows the opposite dynamic. When Yahweh hears the people's cry (צַעֲקָתָם שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי), He responds with compassion and plans their deliverance. The only instance of Yahweh's anger in this passage occurs when Moses voices his own personal objections and concerns (פִּ 'Send by the hand of whom You will send'), not when the people voice their opinions. When the people encounter Yahweh's signs through Moses, they believe and worship (וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ), which elicits no divine anger. The passage demonstrates Yahweh's anger responding to an individual's resistance, not to the collective voicing of opinions.
